questions.question: How do CSS custom properties work — inheritance, cascading, and the theme/runtime patterns they enable?
questions.title: Css Custom Properties
questions.direct_answer: Custom properties (--name: value) are CASCADE-PARTICIPATING, INHERITED variables — unlike preprocessor variables (compile-time, lexical): they resolve at computed-value time per element, so :root-declared values inherit everywhere and can be OVERRIDDEN at any subtree (the theming mechanism: [data-theme='dark'] { --bg: ... } cascades to everything inside). Usage: var(--x) with a fallback chain var(--x, var(--y), 10px). They power: design tokens (a :root scale consumed by components), runtime theming (dark mode = swap a handful of custom properties at a data-attribute or class — zero re-render), JS-driven values (el.style.setProperty('--x', v) — the sanctioned channel for JS state into CSS, consumed by transforms/animations), and responsive theming (media/container queries REASSIGN tokens: @media (min-width: 60rem) { :root { --space: 1.5rem } }).

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DEF['--token: value'] -->|cascade + inherit| SCOPE[:root → subtree override]
    SCOPE --> USE[var(--token, fallback) — full expression allowed]
    TH[data-theme dark] --> SWAP[reassign ~10 tokens — instant theme]
    JS[el.style.setProperty('--x', v)] --> LIVE[runtime channel into CSS]
    MQ[media / container query] --> RESPO[reassign tokens responsively]
    PRE[$sass var] --> COMPILE[compile-time — no runtime swap, no JS access]
    INVALID[invalid at computed time] --> INIT[falls to property initial value — not prior rule]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The registered-properties upgrade (the typed half): @property --x { syntax: '<length>'; inherits: false; initial-value: 0px } makes a custom property a REAL registered property — type-checked at parse time, ANIMATABLE (the huge win: unregistered custom properties interpolate as discrete 'flip' at 50%, registered ones tween), non-inheriting when declared so. This is what makes runtime-animated themes and gradient-angle animations possible in pure CSS — the feature behind modern loaders/progress bars that animate token VALUES.

The inheritance control points (where scoping bites): inherited-by-default means a --radius set on :root reaches EVERY component — overrides inside a card propagate to its children too (usually wanted for theming, a leak when it's component-local state: the fix is declaring at the component scope, or @property inherits: false for a registered token). The companion gotcha: custom properties DO inherit into shadow DOM from the host's ancestors (the deliberate cross-boundary channel — the sanctioned way to theme third-party web components), while normal properties hit the shadow boundary.

The token architecture pattern (the systems-level answer): design tokens as custom properties is the bridge between design-tool tokens (Figma variables) and code: primitive scale at :root (--blue-500, --space-2), semantic aliases at the theme layer (--color-action: var(--blue-600) — 'the button color' name), component-local references consuming ONLY semantic tokens. The separation is what lets a rebrand change primitives without touching components, and theming (light/dark/brand-per-tenant) reassigns semantics only. Name that three-layer architecture and the 'how do you scale CSS theming' interview question is answered.
